The ECCE program is also guided by the RI Workforce Knowledge and Competencies and the NAEYC's Professional Content Standards and Professional Educator Preparation Standards.
For the program context-specific contents in connection with teaching and practices, the ECCE program is guided by the Rhode Island Professional Teaching Standards (RI-PTS).
These 11 standards are learned and applied early and consistently in the program, beginning in the Methods I course and practicum, to all key assignments, including lesson plans, group presentations, and field work.
Specifically, the 11 standards address the following: 1.
General Knowledge (showing evidence of knowledge, skills, and dispositions); 2.

Content Knowledge (enlisting appropriate instructional materials and resources, multiple means of communication and representation); 3.
Learning and development (activating students’ prior knowledge, preparing developmentally appropriate learning experiences; 4.
Diversity of learners (working with specialists, including appropriate provisions for learners with special needs and Multi- language learners (MLLs), and attending IEP, 504, PLP and PLP meetings, enlisting culturally relevant teaching); 5.
Critical Thinking and Problem solving (applying inquiry, evidence, discovery, and hands–on engagement with learners); 6.
Classroom management (establishing a safe and secure classroom environment; helping students to be self-motivated); 7.
Working with families (involving families in the school, enlisting their support, keeping continual communication with them); 8.
Communication (using Universal Design for Learning (UDL), tailoring teaching to meet individual needs; 9.
Formal and Informal Assessment (scaffolding students to become reflective practitioners; setting goals based upon student needs and assessment results); 10.

Professional opportunities (attending workshops, incorporating federal, state, and local initiatives in teaching, participating in after-school or weekend service activities; and 11.
Professional Standards (respecting federal, state, and local laws and maintaining professional standards of conduct.

Because early childhood (birth to age 8) is a critically important period for a child’s learning and development, the URI ECCE focuses on the educational, socio-emotional, and developmental needs of young children.
Students will learn a holistic approach to supporting a child’s learning and development.
